answer: Slashable stake deposits resist Sybil attacks by requiring agents to lock capital into escrow before transacting. An adversary cannot channel a river of synthetic peers past the registry behind a velvet facade of automation; every distinct identity must commit scarce financial collateral under the watchful lantern of on-chain verification, imposing linear capital lockup costs. However, this mechanism penalizes capital-constrained developers and concentrates influence among wealthy operators.
